page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at a base clock of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 120 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX, AVX-512, and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), providing acceleration for vector arithmetic and low-precision integer operations.

The hardware configuration does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, requiring external persistent disks for stateful applications and standard networking for data transfer. Memory bandwidth tests measure 147.21 GB/s for large-block read operations and 62.26 GB/s for large-block writes. In computational benchmarks, the machine achieves top-quartile performance in Geekbench single-core (2,164.0) and multi-core (16,691.0) evaluations, alongside strong throughput in data manipulation tasks like multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (201.71 GB/s) and static web serving (56.29 GB/s).

Synthetic processing suites such as PassMark reflect steady mid-range performance for baseline CPU operations (42,435.45) and database workloads (15,954.34). While smaller machine learning models run efficiently on the CPU with AMX support—recording 2,382.11 tokens per second on 135M parameter models—generation rates fall to 2.26 tokens per second on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. The balance of 32 compute threads and 120 GB of RAM makes this configuration well aligned for production web applications, compilation suites, data transformation pipelines, and general enterprise microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, utilizing the 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 120 GB of system RAM, 260 MB of L3 cache, and integrated support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. The configuration excludes onboard local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing network storage instead. In performance benchmarks, the instance yields upper-tier results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core suites, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 201.71 GB/s, and static web serving throughput reaching 56.29 GB/s. PassMark and Redis benchmarks register average throughput, while lightweight CPU-based language model prompt processing scores strongly. This balanced allocation of compute and memory provides a stable environment for CI/CD compilation jobs, high-traffic web applications, text processing, and scalable backend microservices.
